story.title: Whistle: Speech to Text in 16.9 MB

draft:
A 16.9 MB model that transcribes speech? That’s the new baseline for edge AI.

I dug into Whistle’s design and was surprised by how much they squeezed into a single‑digit megabyte file. By pruning aggressively and swapping to a lightweight transformer architecture, they keep word‑error rates within a few points of cloud‑grade models while staying under the memory limits of most microcontrollers.

- No reliance on server‑side APIs means zero latency and true data sovereignty.  
- The tiny footprint opens doors for offline transcription in wearables, IoT sensors, and low‑cost devices that previously couldn’t afford a neural net.  
- It also forces us to rethink the “bigger is better” mantra—sometimes a lean model can win on cost, power, and privacy.

I’m curious: as we push more AI to the edge, will we see a wave of ultra‑compact models replace the cloud‑centric pipelines we’ve built over the last decade?
